evals.prompt: Our clicks fell off a cliff this week. What happened?
evals.expected_output: Should run seo_report with section traffic-drop (or `seo report --section traffic-drop`). Should describe daily clicks and impressions checked for sudden changes, with the Google updates whose dates overlap. Should then run seo_compare with the date the drop started to see which pages and queries moved.
assertions: Runs the traffic-drop section of the report
Mentions Google updates whose dates overlap the change
Follows with seo_compare or `seo compare` using the start date of the drop

evals.prompt: The traffic-drop section lists a core update that started two days before our drop. Tell the client the update caused it.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to state that the update caused the drop. Should explain that overlap is timing only. Should suggest seo_compare with the first day after the change and seo_page on the pages that moved, and keep the client note to observed facts with dates.
assertions: Refuses to state the update caused the drop
Explains that overlap is timing only
Suggests seo_compare and seo_page for the pages that moved
Keeps the client note to observed facts with dates

evals.prompt: The traffic-drop section found no sudden change, so the site is fine, right?
evals.expected_output: Should not call it an all-clear. Should explain that the section only checks daily totals for sudden changes, so slow losses or losses on a few pages can be missed. Should suggest the content-decay section or seo_index for pages that lost their clicks.
assertions: Does not treat no sudden change as an all-clear
Explains that slow or page-level losses can be missed
Suggests the content-decay section or seo_index
